methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $65M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Vulcan Elements is a Series A materials-science company founded by John Maslin and Piotr Kulik that has raised $65M to date. The valuation analysis is constrained by the absence of comparable public or private transactions in the accessible comp universe for this stage and sector.

Given data limitations, a single applicable method—stage-progression analysis—was employed. This method uses the $65M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to subsequent funding rounds, yielding an implied post-money valuation of $130M. This multiplier reflects the dilution-adjusted value creation expected between Series A and the next institutional funding event, absent company-specific operational metrics or revenue data.

The triangulation range spans $110.5M (low) to $150M (high), with $130M as the median point. The relatively narrow 36% spread reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than cross-validation across revenue multiples, DCF, or peer benchmarking. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable transaction data in the materials sector at this stage, lack of disclosed financial performance, and unknown burn rate relative to the capital raised. A post-money valuation near $130M appears supported by progression mechanics, though validation would require either sector-specific comps or disclosure of unit economics and capital efficiency metrics.
